title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_0LD1LB_1LA1LF_0LB0RD_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_0LD1LB_1LA1LF_0LB0RD_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the twelve shift rules that make the leftward sweep turn v-words into u-words. The tape is a growing run of v on the left and a region of u-blocks separated by short markers on the right whose sizes form a counter-like hierarchy; the rule by which the markers move was not derived. The machine halts only on 1 D> 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Shift rules: v becomes u going left
claims.text: Leftward, B, C, D and F cross runs of the rotations of v = 10100100 and leave the matching rotations of u = 11111010; A and B cross (01)n and (10)n rightward, B and C fill them with 1s leftward.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: Only F reading 1 halts; F is entered only from D reading 1 (1LF), so the machine halts exactly on 1 D> 1. Read off the table.

claims.title: The tape at step 10<sup>9</sup>
claims.text: v1269 0 1 0 v392 1 0 [A0] 1 0 1 0 u859 13 0 1 0 u208 13 0 1 0 u208 12 u992 16 u234 ... u98 13 0 1 0 u44 13 0 1 0 u44 12 u46 ... u23 12 u23 ... u11 ... u10 ... u11 ... 19: the u-blocks come in groups of about three similar sizes, each group about half the size of the one before.

claims.title: A bouncer with a counter
claims.text: The visited tape grows like the square root of time at the left end; the markers between u-blocks drift (the dark curves of the space-time diagram) and their spacings halve from group to group, the pattern of a binary counter stored in the gaps. Observed only.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl K = 3..6 leaves halting configurations; n-gram CPS 3 to 7 fails; no invariant mod 2..12.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,247 cells have been visited and 30,463 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.011).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The halting pattern 1 D> 1 could arise at the markers between u-blocks or at the turn; the markers' rule (how a group of gaps is rewritten when the head passes) was not derived.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0RA0LC_0RA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 47,247 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Two 8-cell words and a row of markers
html:
Write v for 10100100 and u for 11111010. At step 109 the tape is

v^1269 0 1 0 v^392 1 0 [A0] 1 0 1 0 u^859 111 0 1 0 u^208 111 0 1 0 u^208 11 u^992 1^6 u^234 ... u^44 111 0 1 0 u^44 11 u^46 ... u^23 11 u^23 ... 1^9

a long run of v on the left (it grows like the square root of time), then a region of u split into blocks by short markers like 111 0 1 0, 11 and 1^6.

sections.heading: Going left, v turns into u
html: Lean proves twelve shift rules: whenever the head runs left over a run of v-words (in any of their rotations, in states B, C, D or F), it leaves u-words behind (lean/Rules.lean). The way back is not a clean shift: the head works through the markers, which is where the block sizes change.

The block sizes of u form a hierarchy: groups of about three nearly equal blocks (44, 44, 46; 22, 23, 23; 11, 10, 11), each group about half the size of the one before. That is the look of a counter whose digits are the gaps. In the space-time diagram the markers are dark curves drifting slowly.

sections.heading: Same first three states, different machine
html: This machine shares states A, B and C with 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_0LD1LB_1LA1LE_0LB0LF_1LD---, whose rounds were decoded into a Collatz-like map. Here the same sweeps over 10 and 11 appear (the shift rules a_right, b_right, b_left, c_left are the same), but D, E and F differ and the tape is organised in 8-cell words instead.

sections.heading: Only on 1 D> 1
html: The machine stops only when F reads a 1, and F is entered only from D reading a 1 and stepping left; so it stops exactly when D reads a 1 that has a 1 on its left. The marker rule decides whether that ever happens; it was not derived.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.494). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.011).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,247 cells (37,015 left of the start, 36 right), with a density of 1s of 0.645.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0LD_0RC1RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LE_0RA0LC_0RA---: rename A→D, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB1RF_1LC0LF_1RD0LB_0RA1RE_1RD---_0RC0LA (in a mirror): 9,999,977 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 9,999,986 there

summary: A bouncer over 8-cell words: going left the head turns v = 10100100 into u = 11111010; the u side carries separators whose spacings shrink by about half from one group to the next, like the digits of a counter; sibling of 1RB0RE_1LC0RA_0LD1LB_1LA1LE_0LB0LF_1LD---.
